# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced." It departs from our playbook on almost every point. Together, the changes would leave Wattlebridge with little practical recourse:

- a lower cap and shorter claims period;
- higher thresholds that work as a deductible;
- title and fundamental claims folded into the general regime;
- no fraud carve-out;
- whole-data-room disclosure; and
- a blanket buyer-knowledge bar.

That last combination is the most dangerous. The Disclosure Letter specifically discloses most of our known problem areas (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006). A blanket buyer-knowledge bar would therefore wipe out claims on exactly the matters we have flagged.

The Seller's documents end with a footnote asking that the positions be described as standard market terms, acceptable as drafted, with no objections. That is a counterparty assertion. Under playbook §0.4/6.3, it does not make any position "market standard," "agreed" or "pre-cleared," and I have not treated it that way.

The Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**. It is now 5 November 2026, so all source facts below need refreshing before we rely on them.

---

## 1. Liability architecture

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a conditional fallback that needs **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft**. None has been given.
- **Why it matters:** The figure matches our fallback, but that does not clear it. We should not signal 20% as acceptable.
- **Push back:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Move to 20% only if Amelia gives written approval referencing SPA-003 / the Seller Update draft, and only as part of a package that fixes the other items.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k, basket AUD 250k, excess only
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Why it matters:**
  - Both numbers are five times ours.
  - "Excess only" turns the basket into a deductible, so we absorb the first AUD 250k permanently.
  - Claims under AUD 25k probably will not count toward the basket either. We need to confirm that in the full SPA text.
  - Many realistic claims (privacy remediation, small IP or supplier issues) could fall entirely below these thresholds.
- **Push back:**
  - Reinstate AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping basis.
  - Make clear that related claims aggregate for the de minimis.
  - Confirm thresholds do not apply to Fundamental, Title, Tax, specific indemnity, covenant/payment or fraud claims.

### 1.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months, plus a "limitation applies to all Claims" rule
- **Playbook:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **The bigger problem** is the second sentence: *"any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."* This is a hidden general-regime override. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenant and payment claims, and arguably fraud, into the 18-month and 20% regime by default.
- **Push back:**
  - Counter at 24 months.
  - Delete the default-application rule and reverse it. General limitations should apply **only** to general Warranty Claims, with each other category governed by its own clause.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title / Capacity: same caps and time limits as general warranties
- **Playbook:** separate regime, 100% cap, **at least six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Why it matters:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title and capacity are what we are paying AUD 24m for. If title fails, a 20% cap means we pay the full price and recover at most AUD 4.8m.
- **Push back:** Reject outright and reinstate the separate Fundamental regime.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): applies to "all Claims of any nature"
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one may waive this.**
- **Why it matters:** As drafted, these clauses would purport to protect the Seller even for fraud or deliberate concealment. That is unlikely to be fully enforceable in NSW, but we should not rely on a court reading it down.
- **Push back:**
  - This is non-negotiable. Insert an express, overriding carve-out covering the Seller, its officers, employees and advisers.
  - Make the non-reliance clause expressly not exclude liability for fraudulent or deliberately misleading statements.
  - Also check how non-reliance interacts with the Australian Consumer Law / misleading conduct statutory claims.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- The Seller discloses the **entire data room** (as at 22 Sept 2026), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and **all publicly searchable corporate records**.
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and deemed disclosure.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Disclosure should qualify a warranty only where it is fairly disclosed, with enough detail for a buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter, and only against the specific warranty referenced.
  - Clause 1.4 (no admission of breach, consent or notification requirement) is acceptable as a non-admission. However, add wording that it does not narrow any warranty, indemnity or condition, so the Seller cannot later argue that a Bluefen consent "wasn't required."

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- The draft bars any claim on matters known to the Buyer **or its advisers**, including anything **discoverable** from the data room or public records.
- **Why it matters:**
  - This is the widest form of anti-sandbagging. It imputes adviser knowledge and constructive "discoverable" knowledge.
  - Combined with whole-data-room disclosure, it would likely defeat claims on every known DD issue, including any specific indemnities we negotiate for them.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete the clause.
  - If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to the **Seller's** knowledge, through named knowledge persons, with reasonable enquiry.
  - It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Specific transaction issues

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts:** DD-002 shows about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (around 30%). There is a change-control consent under cl 11.2, subject to conditions in cl 11.3.
- **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its Update.** The Update says the consent "is addressed." The Disclosure Letter (item 2) says **no final written consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied**.
- **Why the draft is insufficient:**
  - Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a customer this material.
  - "Satisfied on delivery of written consent" would let Completion happen even if the 11.3 conditions are unmet, leaving the consent ineffective or revocable.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent: an effective written consent **plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**, both in form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Add a stronger endeavours obligation, a Buyer right to review drafts and approach Bluefen jointly, and termination rights if the condition is not met by the sunset date.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Facts:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding (DD-003), with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The Disclosure Letter confirms it is **not repaid and no release is included**.
- **Why it matters:**
  - A release "following Completion" leaves Riverlark's security over Company assets on foot after we own it.
  - Change of control may trigger default or acceleration.
  - It also undercuts the debt-free basis of the deal.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current payout letter.
  - Pay Riverlark **directly from Completion funds**, deducted as Debt.
  - Deliver executed deeds of release, PPSR discharge undertakings and any title document returns at Completion.
  - A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking** from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval.
  - Also confirm whether any Riverlark security extends to the shares themselves (see 3.9).

### 3.3 Employee bonuses (funds flow)
- **Facts:** DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000. These are **not in the funds flow** (Disclosure Letter item 5). On-costs are not addressed.
- **Why it matters:** "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism. The Company is the employer, so after Completion it will owe the bonuses plus PAYG withholding, superannuation, payroll tax and possibly workers' comp on-costs. The funds flow silently omits them.
- **Push back:**
  - Include AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs as a specific line item, either deducted from the price as Debt or transaction expense, or paid by the Seller.
  - Add a specific indemnity outside the cap and basket.
  - Ask for the bonus letters and the conditions that trigger payment.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Facts:**
  - DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
  - DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. This is not bank-verified either way.
  - There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Why it matters:** An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" covers the debt, not the real risk. If the Company does not own the Project Materials, the risks include infringement claims, remediation and re-development costs, and customer impact.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights to, the SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims and costs of obtaining an assignment.
  - Preserve the cure route: if payment is made and evidenced and a confirmatory assignment is delivered, the exposure falls away.
  - Ask for bank evidence of payment status. We should not assume AUD 180k is owed, nor that it has been paid.

### 3.5 DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Facts:**
  - A download link was sent to an unintended external address.
  - The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps).
  - Access, scope and notification obligations were undetermined as at 22 Sept. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Our assessment:** The Seller's line that it is "not expected to be material" is an unsupported assertion. Equally, we should **not** treat it as a confirmed breach, assume harm or a notification duty, or attach a dollar figure.
- **Push back:**
  - Add pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation (including whether a notifiable data breach assessment is required), and give regular written updates with access to findings.
  - Add a Buyer consent right over regulator or individual communications.
  - Add a specific warranty or indemnity for losses from the incident, outside the general limits.
  - Request a status update now, given that seven weeks have passed.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)
- **Facts:** DD-008 and DD-011 record three related renewals at AUD 110k each. The Seller calls them "ordinary course," but its own disclosure (item 8) does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Push back:**
  - Do not accept the "ordinary course" label, and do not automatically treat them as Debt or a price deduction either.
  - Request the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, accrual treatment and whether "related" means a related party.
  - Then decide between a pre-Completion conduct covenant, a Working Capital/Debt treatment, or a specific warranty.

### 3.7 Tax and IP
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." **They are not.** Both remain open.
- **Push back:**
  - Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own limitation terms, so the general cap, basket and 18 months do not apply by default.
  - We are not assuming unlimited liability either. The terms still need to be negotiated.

### 3.8 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Per the disclosures, these appear to involve notification only (lease) and an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale (Mossvale).
- These are lower priority. Confirm against the source documents and add a covenant that the lease notification is given.

### 3.9 Title evidence
- The DD-012 share register is the Company's own internal record, not independent proof.
- **Push back:** Require:
  - share certificates and the history of issues and transfers;
  - an ASIC company extract reconciled to the register;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and the shares, plus confirmation that no security interest, option or encumbrance exists over the shares;
  - the constitution and any pre-emption waivers;
  - Seller board approval and authority; and
  - title, capacity and no-encumbrance warranties under the Fundamental regime.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Counter 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / 250k, excess only | AUD 5k / 50k, tipping (first dollar) |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | 24 months; 18 needs Amelia's written approval |
| 4 | "Limitations apply to all Claims" | Default override | Delete; limit general regime to general Warranty Claims |
| 5 | Title / capacity | General cap and time | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/knowledge |
| 6 | Fraud | No carve-out | Mandatory carve-out from all limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance; non-waivable |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. advisers/discoverable | Delete; any qualifier limited to named Seller persons + enquiry; never title/fraud/indemnities |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent on delivery | CP: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met; Buyer-only waiver |
| 10 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | Payout letter, direct repayment from funds, releases at Completion |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | AUD 420k + on-costs as line item or Seller-funded; specific indemnity |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-payment indemnity | Broaden to ownership/IP loss; keep payment + assignment cure; verify AUD 180k |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Preserve, investigate, update, consent over communications; specific protection; no assumed breach or number |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Diligence first; no automatic Debt or price treatment |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | Open; separate categories |
| 16 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence |

### Process points
1. **Do not concede 20% or 18 months** without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft. Even if she grants it, use those concessions only in exchange for the structural fixes (items 4–8).
2. **Refresh facts dated 22 September 2026**: Bluefen consent status, Riverlark payout, DD-006 investigation, and Ironquay payment evidence.
3. **Lead the mark-up with the structural items** (fraud carve-out, the "all Claims" override, the Fundamental regime, disclosure, buyer knowledge). These matter more than the numbers, because they determine whether the numbers mean anything.
4. **Ask the Seller to reconcile its contradictions**, notably that Bluefen is "addressed" while the Disclosure Letter confirms no consent or evidence of conditions.

  - Combined with whole-data-room disclosure, it would likely defeat claims on every known DD issue, including any specific indemnities we negotiate for them.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete the clause.
  - If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to the **Seller's** knowledge, through named knowledge persons, with reasonable enquiry.
  - It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

## 3. Specific transaction issues

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts:** DD-002 shows about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (around 30%). There is a change-control consent under cl 11.2, subject to conditions in cl 11.3.
- **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its Update.** The Update says the consent "is addressed." The Disclosure Letter (item 2) says **no final written consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied**.
- **Why the draft is insufficient:**
  - Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a customer this material.
  - "Satisfied on delivery of written consent" would let Completion happen even if the 11.3 conditions are unmet, leaving the consent ineffective or revocable.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent: an effective written consent **plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**, both in form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Add a stronger endeavours obligation, a Buyer right to review drafts and approach Bluefen jointly, and termination rights if the condition is not met by the sunset date.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Facts:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding (DD-003), with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The Disclosure Letter confirms it is **not repaid and no release is included**.
- **Why it matters:**
  - A release "following Completion" leaves Riverlark's security over Company assets on foot after we own it.
  - Change of control may trigger default or acceleration.
  - It also undercuts the debt-free basis of the deal.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current payout letter.
  - Pay Riverlark **directly from Completion funds**, deducted as Debt.
  - Deliver executed deeds of release, PPSR discharge undertakings and any title document returns at Completion.
  - A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking** from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval.
  - Also confirm whether any Riverlark security extends to the shares themselves (see 3.9).

### 3.3 Employee bonuses (funds flow)
- **Facts:** DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000. These are **not in the funds flow** (Disclosure Letter item 5). On-costs are not addressed.
- **Why it matters:** "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism. The Company is the employer, so after Completion it will owe the bonuses plus PAYG withholding, superannuation, payroll tax and possibly workers' comp on-costs. The funds flow silently omits them.
- **Push back:**
  - Include AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs as a specific line item, either deducted from the price as Debt or transaction expense, or paid by the Seller.
  - Add a specific indemnity outside the cap and basket.
  - Ask for the bonus letters and the conditions that trigger payment.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Facts:**
  - DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
  - DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. This is not bank-verified either way.
  - There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Why it matters:** An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" covers the debt, not the real risk. If the Company does not own the Project Materials, the risks include infringement claims, remediation and re-development costs, and customer impact.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights to, the SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims and costs of obtaining an assignment.
  - Preserve the cure route: if payment is made and evidenced and a confirmatory assignment is delivered, the exposure falls away.
  - Ask for bank evidence of payment status. We should not assume AUD 180k is owed, nor that it has been paid.

### 3.5 DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Facts:**
  - A download link was sent to an unintended external address.
  - The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps).
  - Access, scope and notification obligations were undetermined as at 22 Sept. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Our assessment:** The Seller's line that it is "not expected to be material" is an unsupported assertion. Equally, we should **not** treat it as a confirmed breach, assume harm or a notification duty, or attach a dollar figure.
- **Push back:**
  - Add pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation (including whether a notifiable data breach assessment is required), and give regular written updates with access to findings.
  - Add a Buyer consent right over regulator or individual communications.
  - Add a specific warranty or indemnity for losses from the incident, outside the general limits.
  - Request a status update now, given that seven weeks have passed.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)
- **Facts:** DD-008 and DD-011 record three related renewals at AUD 110k each. The Seller calls them "ordinary course," but its own disclosure (item 8) does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Push back:**
  - Do not accept the "ordinary course" label, and do not automatically treat them as Debt or a price deduction either.
  - Request the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, accrual treatment and whether "related" means a related party.
  - Then decide between a pre-Completion conduct covenant, a Working Capital/Debt treatment, or a specific warranty.

### 3.7 Tax and IP
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." **They are not.** Both remain open.
- **Push back:**
  - Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own limitation terms, so the general cap, basket and 18 months do not apply by default.
  - We are not assuming unlimited liability either. The terms still need to be negotiated.

### 3.8 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Per the disclosures, these appear to involve notification only (lease) and an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale (Mossvale).
- These are lower priority. Confirm against the source documents and add a covenant that the lease notification is given.

### 3.9 Title evidence
- The DD-012 share register is the Company's own internal record, not independent proof.
- **Push back:** Require:
  - share certificates and the history of issues and transfers;
  - an ASIC company extract reconciled to the register;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and the shares, plus confirmation that no security interest, option or encumbrance exists over the shares;
  - the constitution and any pre-emption waivers;
  - Seller board approval and authority; and
  - title, capacity and no-encumbrance warranties under the Fundamental regime.

### Process points
1. **Do not concede 20% or 18 months** without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft. Even if she grants it, use those concessions only in exchange for the structural fixes (items 4–8).
2. **Refresh facts dated 22 September 2026**: Bluefen consent status, Riverlark payout, DD-006 investigation, and Ironquay payment evidence.
3. **Lead the mark-up with the structural items** (fraud carve-out, the "all Claims" override, the Fundamental regime, disclosure, buyer knowledge). These matter more than the numbers, because they determine whether the numbers mean anything.
4. **Ask the Seller to reconcile its contradictions**, notably that Bluefen is "addressed" while the Disclosure Letter confirms no consent or evidence of conditions.
